minutes.headline: Committee debated whether to follow the town's recent project rejections or press its own master-plan vision.
minutes.summary: The Master Plan Steering Committee spent most of the meeting working through consultant Ramy's (Overunder) strategy matrix line by line, accepting, rejecting or reworking items on housing, business advertising, community gardens, sidewalks/crosswalks, sustainability, and building reuse. It also confronted process problems (missing data from the consultant, no town planner, open-meeting-law limits on sharing opinions), reorganized its own officers, and set a biweekly meeting schedule aiming for a completed draft by Thanksgiving.

budget_items.topic: Database of available commercial spaces (advertise vacant spaces for sale/lease)
budget_items.what_was_said: A member asked whether there is a budget line item for a database of available commercial spaces; Ramy said the cost would be fairly low and the effort fairly quick.

A member asked whether the town could get grants from MassDOT to help fund sidewalk projects; another member said the committee has a spreadsheet of funding opportunities but wasn't sure it covered this specific project.

budget_items.topic: Green-community grants tied to the stretch energy code
budget_items.what_was_said: A member said the town's adoption of the stretch energy code, as part of its green-community status, has opened it up to additional grant funding, including for street lights.

Ramy/Overunder has been retained for roughly two years to write the master plan, longer than the typical process cited, and a member said they had not been shown the actual contract language defining the deliverables.
A member noted the town's contract planning director works limited hours per week and remotely, and can offer no additional support to this committee's work.

decisions.decision: Quorum for the committee was reduced to five members via a prior binding board vote, easing future scheduling.
Tentative consensus to mark the 'advertise vacant spaces for sale/lease' item as accepted alongside the zoning-barrier review, pending wording (later contested).
Leaned toward rewording the item so the town encourages a dialogue with commercial realtors about vacant spaces, rather than the town itself advertising them.
Agreed to sort matrix items into 'must have' versus 'nice to have' categories before finalizing recommendations.
Accepted the community-garden strategy for the master plan.
Accepted the year-round-programming-of-gathering-spaces strategy, with a request to add concrete examples for the consultant.
Agreed the 'use empty town buildings for after-school activities' item needs a preceding overall plan for the town's vacant buildings.
Agreed to keep the universally accessible playground strategy in the master plan despite its tie to the currently unfunded Marshall Park project.
Agreed to add 'crosswalks' alongside 'sidewalks' in the walkability strategy language.
Agreed to keep language about the town continuing to be a 'green community' under the stretch energy code.
Informally set Thanksgiving as the target date for a completed master-plan draft, with no hard deadline.
Agreed to try to meet bi-weekly, on the second and fourth Wednesday of the month at 6 p.m.
Confirmed the roster no longer includes Parks & Recreation or one at-large seat, and is still missing Conservation Commission and Zoning Board of Appeals representatives.
Agreed on draft wording for a public-access cable channel announcement slide about the committee.

what_happened.line: The committee elected a new chair, vice chair and clerk and adopted a biweekly meeting schedule.

Members worked through the consultant's strategy matrix, accepting items on community gardens, walkability and green-community status while rejecting or reworking others on vacant buildings and business advertising.
A prior board vote lowered the committee's quorum to five members, easing the scheduling gaps that had stalled its work.
The committee set an informal target of a completed master-plan draft by Thanksgiving, with no hard deadline.
Members said missing data from the consultant and the town having no dedicated planner continue to slow the process.

why_it_matters: The master plan being assembled here can shape future zoning, sidewalk and building-reuse decisions residents will eventually vote on at town meeting.
Items accepted or rejected in the strategy matrix -- community gardens, walkability, vacant-building use -- indicate what the town's next long-range plan will and will not recommend.
A resident asking about a specific project (a park, a sidewalk, a vacant building) can check whether it appears in this matrix as accepted, rejected, or still pending rework.
watch_next: Next meetings on the second and fourth Wednesday at 6 p.m., working toward a target (not binding) Thanksgiving draft completion
